facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI (Registo Civil Integrado), introduced in 2023, is a web-based system with a centralised database in which the birth is entered at the CR post, the Unique Citizen Number being assigned as registration begins, and which is interconnected with other CR posts and the civil and criminal identification database.

The World Bank diagnostic states that from 2023 births are registered in RCI at the CR posts equipped with it, which issue a birth registration receipt carrying the Unique Citizen Number; it describes no death registration in RCI.

The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI, piloted in four Luanda registries, is in all registry offices in Luanda except Cacuaco's and in one CR post each in Huambo, Benguela and Lubango, with plans to extend it country-wide; it gives no count of RCI offices, and puts Luanda province at 39 CR units and the country at at least 255 CR units in 2023 (DNIRN data). The coverage is undated; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights (MINJUSDH) developed the new civil registration information system integrated with the identity card issuance system, and that a PGIBI back-office official checks each RCI registration.

The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI was developed by a private firm and that the government remains dependent on that private entity for all future developments of it. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.
The World Bank diagnostic states that RCI was introduced in 2023, went from a four-registry pilot to all of Luanda's civil registry and is being gradually expanded to other provinces.

The World Bank diagnostic states that SIRC is a web-based civil registration system with no central database and no connection between the CR units using it, each unit running its own infrastructure and local server. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that SIRC is used for civil registration and the issue of its documents, birth certificates included, computerised units issuing a birth registration receipt; it describes no death registration in SIRC. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that only the CR offices in Luanda, the provincial capitals and some municipalities, about half of the maternity clinic posts and the mobile registration kits are computerised, and that outside Luanda and one office each in Huambo, Benguela and Huíla the systems are not interconnected; it gives no count of computerised offices against at least 255 CR units in 2023. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that SIRC is maintained on request by MINJUSDH's Information and Communications Technology Cabinet or its provincial delegations, and that there is a vendor lock-in, the source code never having been made available to the government. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that the Programme for the Modernization, Simplification and Computerization of Registry and Notary Services was launched in 2006 (Council of Ministers Resolution 39/06 of 17 July 2006) to computerise all civil registration and notary offices, a software contract followed in 2008 and SIRC was then rolled out in Luanda and the provincial capitals.

The World Bank diagnostic states that registration posts in maternity clinics and mobile units with computerised kits run a localised SIRC on a standalone machine with no interface to the CR office, the data being copied to an external disk, typically every six months, and uploaded to the SIRC database in the CR office. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.
facts.system: SIRC (localised version at maternity posts and mobile units)

facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that the maternity registration posts were funded by UNICEF, that funding fell short once the project support ended, and that most of the 70 posts set up across 8 provinces are inactive, the government working to reactivate them. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.
facts.system: SIRC (localised version at maternity posts and mobile units)

facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that the majority of civil registration units still rely on paper-based records and that many retain paper processes, most offices being concentrated in urban centres; its example is Bembe municipality in Uíge, served by one non-computerised registration service. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that when a birth is registered at a rural CR post or health facility the pre-registration document must be forwarded to the appropriate CR office, which processes the certificate and records the information in paper ledgers or in a database. No date is given; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.

The World Bank diagnostic states that PROMOREN, a web-based civil registration system with a centralised database and biometric capture, used in two interconnected CR offices in Luanda and in the mobile units of the Massification project, is no longer used, the developer's technical assistance having been discontinued. The withdrawal is undated; dated to the diagnostic's 2024 revision.
